issues: Sequential scan on 'cast_info' with a non-SARGable filter `(ci.note ~~ '%(voice)%' AND ci.note ~~ '%(uncredited)%')` reads over 12 million rows to find approximately 10,000. A GIN index using the pg_trgm extension on the 'note' column would significantly improve performance.
Significant row underestimation for the join between 'cast_info' and 'role_type' (planned: 51, actual: 8,625), leading to suboptimal plan choices.
The filter `(cn.country_code)::text = '[ru]'::text` is applied after an index scan on 'company_name', resulting in many wasted lookups. An index on 'country_code' could be beneficial.
The filter `(t.production_year > 2005)` is applied after an index scan on 'title', which is inefficient. An index on 'production_year' could improve performance if the planner reorders the joins.
advice: Create a GIN index on `cast_info.note` using the `pg_trgm` extension to accelerate the `LIKE` filters.
Add indexes on `title(production_year)` and `company_name(country_code)` to improve filtering performance.
Rewrite the query using explicit `JOIN` syntax for better readability and to eliminate a redundant join condition.
Run `ANALYZE` on the involved tables after creating indexes to update statistics, which helps the query planner choose a more optimal execution plan.
optimized_sql:
-- Step 1: Create indexes (run once)
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

-- Index for LIKE filters on cast_info.note
CREATE INDEX idx_ci_note_trgm ON cast_info USING gin (note gin_trgm_ops);

-- Index for filter on company_name.country_code
CREATE INDEX idx_cn_country_code ON company_name (country_code);

-- Index for filter on title.production_year
CREATE INDEX idx_t_production_year ON title (production_year);


-- Step 2: Run the optimized query
SELECT MIN(chn.name) AS uncredited_voiced_character,
       MIN(t.title) AS russian_movie
FROM title AS t
JOIN cast_info AS ci ON t.id = ci.movie_id
JOIN movie_companies AS mc ON t.id = mc.movie_id
JOIN role_type AS rt ON ci.role_id = rt.id
JOIN char_name AS chn ON ci.person_role_id = chn.id
JOIN company_name AS cn ON mc.company_id = cn.id
JOIN company_type AS ct ON mc.company_type_id = ct.id
WHERE ci.note LIKE '%(voice)%'
  AND ci.note LIKE '%(uncredited)%'
  AND cn.country_code = '[ru]'
  AND rt.role = 'actor'
  AND t.production_year > 2005;
